//AzureLowSpeed: The STANDARD general-purpose storage account (musicsalesstorageaccount). Audio transcoding runs in the MusicSalesApp.Functions Azure Functions app, and its queues plus the upload staging container live here - the premium account in the Azure section offers no Queue service at all. One section per storage account, so its connection string exists once. Real values live in the gitignored appsettings.{Environment}.json.
//MediaProcessingApiKey: Shared secret the audio-processing Function presents on its callbacks to api/media-processing/*. Must NOT be the same value as MobileApiKey - that one ships inside a distributed mobile app, this one authorises writes to the song catalogue.
//LyricsFunctions: The SECOND Function app - Python on Linux, Flex Consumption - which aligns pasted lyrics to a song's audio (Demucs for vocal separation, then forced alignment). Separate from the audio Function app because a Function app is pinned to one language runtime. Unlike that one it is invoked over HTTP rather than through a queue: a Durable HTTP starter answers with the orchestration's instance id and its management URLs, which a queue trigger has no way to hand back, and that id is what lets the reconciler ask Azure how a run is going instead of guessing from a timestamp. Leave both values blank to disable lyric timing in an environment - the feature reports itself unavailable and nothing else changes. Real values live in the gitignored appsettings.{Environment}.json; Provision-LyricsFunctionApp.ps1 prints them after creating the app.

LyricsFunctions.//FunctionKey: Sent as x-functions-key when starting an orchestration, so it authorises THIS app to the Function app - the opposite direction from MediaProcessingApiKey, and therefore a different secret.

//Likes: RequireStreamBeforeRating gates ONLY the server-side rejection of a like/dislike on a song the user has never streamed; both the Blazor buttons and the MAUI app gate themselves client-side regardless, so turning this off does not put the rule back the way it was for them. It exists for the window where a new server is live but the mobile release is still in App Store / Play review: an app built before this rule reads a 403 as permanently non-retryable and drops the user's rating without saying why - silently, and for good, if it was queued offline. Leave it false until the store releases are out, then set it true to close the direct-API bypass. Absent means true, so a fresh environment is strict by default.
